notes: United Kingdom government policy publications. GOV.UK is the single domain for government services and information.

data.description: UK's data protection law. Incorporates the EU GDPR as UK GDPR via the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018. Supplemented by national provisions covering law enforcement, intelligence services, and exceptions. Enforced by the ICO.
data.notes: Post-Brexit divergence pending via the UK Data (Use and Access) Bill 2024.

data.description: UK law imposing duties of care on online platforms regarding illegal content and content harmful to children. Enforced by Ofcom.
data.notes: Status: In force (Royal Assent October 26, 2023; phased commencement through 2025-2026; verified as of 2026-11-04). Amended in April 2026 to explicitly regulate AI chatbots: Section 216A (inserted by the Crime and Policing Act 2026, s. 248) empowers the Secretary of State to bring standalone AI chatbot providers and AI content-generation tools within OSA scope, and Section 214A (inserted by the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026, s. 70) empowers regulations restricting or preventing children's access to high-risk interactive or AI features.

match_nodes.description: Crime and Policing Act 2026 (including s. 248 / OSA s. 216A AI chatbot powers)

data.description: UK Act of Parliament reforming criminal justice, policing, and online offences; Section 248 inserts Section 216A into the Online Safety Act 2023 to bring standalone AI chatbots and AI-generated content providers within statutory online-safety regulation.
data.notes: Status: In force (Royal Assent April 2026; 2026 c. 20; verified as of 2026-11-04). Section 248 (introduced during parliamentary passage as government amendment New Clause NC120) inserts Section 216A into the Online Safety Act 2023, closing the OSA gap for one-to-one AI chatbot interactions that did not previously qualify as user-to-user or search services.

data.description: UK Act of Parliament on child protection and education; Section 70 inserts Section 214A into the Online Safety Act 2023 enabling secondary regulations to restrict, time-limit, or prevent children's access to specified services or interactive AI chatbot features of concern.
data.notes: Status: In force (Royal Assent April 2026; 2026 c. 21; verified as of 2026-11-04).

data.description: UK's foundational computer-crime law. Criminalises unauthorised access (Section 1), unauthorised access with intent to commit further offences (Section 2), unauthorised modification (Section 3), and making/supplying tools for offences (Section 3A).
data.notes: Reform consultation ongoing (Home Office, 2023+) — possible new defence for legitimate security researchers.

match_nodes.description: Network and Information Systems Regulations 2018 (UK NIS)

data.description: UK implementation of the original EU NIS Directive (now superseded in EU by NIS2). Covers Operators of Essential Services (OES) and Relevant Digital Service Providers (RDSPs).
data.notes: Pending modernisation via the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill announced 2024.

data.description: UK government plan for AI adoption and governance.
data.notes: Published January 2025. Policy direction, not binding legislation. Based on Matt Clifford's independent review. Covers AI infrastructure (compute, data), skills and talent, government adoption of AI, and regulatory approach. Emphasizes pro-innovation regulatory framework rather than comprehensive AI legislation.

data.description: Proposed UK legislation (not yet enacted as of registration), sponsored by the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT), expanding UK NIS Regulations 2018 (secid:regulation/gov.uk/nis-regs-2018) coverage to more digital services/supply chains, with stronger regulator enforcement and incident-reporting powers, and covering managed service providers.
data.notes: Status: Proposed (in progress; not yet Royal Assent; verified as of 2026-11-04). Revisit once enacted.

data.description: Published by DSIT/Central Digital and Data Office. A structured template for publicly documenting how an algorithmic/AI tool used by a public sector body works, its data, oversight, and risks — the UK's answer to a public AI system-card registry. Mandatory since February 2024 for UK government departments/public bodies using algorithmic tools affecting the public.

match_nodes.description: Critical Third Parties regime (financial sector operational resilience)

data.official_name: Operational Resilience: Critical Third Parties to the UK Financial Sector
data.description: Joint rules from the Bank of England, Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA), and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), under powers granted by the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023. Designates and regulates systemically important third-party service providers (cloud/tech vendors) to UK financial firms — operational resilience, incident notification, and testing requirements.
data.notes: Effective January 2025. Publishing bodies (Bank of England, PRA, FCA) do not yet have their own SecID entity entries -- this citation lives under the general gov.uk namespace as a sweep placeholder.
